finding: A hand-written code agent with no reasoning (the Simple Reflex Agent) that replays fixed example probes and compares outputs to the known reference gets perfect identification at k=1 and for additive fault sets. No tested LLM could produce equivalent probes on its own. Gap 4: running the simulation and comparison in code beats doing it in the model.
numbers: Reflex agent V=1.0 (k=1 and additive k+). LLM overall: kernel detection VK 0.65, exact attribution VA 0.28, VA given VK=1 is 0.39 (13 LLMs, k in {1,2}, 3 prompt levels, 5 reps).
quote: By construction, these probes... serve as an analytical oracle that yields perfect identification and attribution accuracy at k = 1
limits: The reflex agent is given the probes by the benchmark designers, so it is an upper bound for deterministic comparison, not a general method. Interacting sets were excluded from this comparison because all models were near 0.
agent_relevance: Put the predict-versus-observe comparison and the probe set in code; let the model only choose which hypothesis to test and read the diff.

finding: Prompt text that already contains discipline rules did not rescue the multiple-fault case. The prompts include rules such as 'a claimed mutation must be supported by a discriminating probe', 'never repeat an uninformative probe', 'do not assume one anomaly explains everything'. Interacting k=2 still collapsed. Gap 7: text guardrails help the easy case, not the hard one.
numbers: Interacting k=2, Level 2 prompt: most of 13 models score 0; only gpt-5.4_medium V=0.20 and gpt-5.4 V=0.07. Hardest cell (minimal prompt plus interacting) average V=0.02. Interacting set average 0.03. Level 0 (most structure and worked example probes) gives substantial gains over Level 1 and 2; weak models fail almost completely without it.
limits: Prompt levels differ in structure and worked examples together, so rule text and example probes are not separated. The interacting test is a small set (one k=2 configuration, n=5 per model).
agent_relevance: Do not count on written rules for the hard multi-fault case. Worked probe examples may matter more than rules; test them apart.

finding: More reasoning effort did not fix the abduction deficit. Moving from low to high effort gave no consistent gain in attribution, and the hardest setting stayed at zero for every effort level.
numbers: Three models (gpt-5.4, gpt-5.5, claude-sonnet-4-6) at low to high effort. Interacting k=2: all failed at every budget, including the highest reasoning-budget setting (accuracy 0). Ladder attribution VA for gpt-5.4: low 0.41, medium 0.47, high 0.46. The k=2 effort test used one mutation configuration, n=5 per model and effort.
limits: Authors call it preliminary and underpowered. Does not test a forced rival-hypothesis step.
agent_relevance: Raising thinking budget is not a substitute for a structural move such as a forced rival hypothesis. Gap 2 stays untested.

finding: Premature commitment is measured: the probe budget is left unused in most attribution failures, so a forced extra step has room to run. Telling the model the fault count changes the error type, not the rate.
numbers: 86.5 percent of cases with correct kernel detected but wrong attribution (VK=1, VA=0) left the probe budget (Pmax 50) unused. Known k leads to hallucinated extra mutations; unknown k leads to omissions. Exact accuracy 0.90 (k=0, null case) vs 0.32 (k=1) vs 0.15 (k=2+) vs 0.03 (interacting).
limits: Observational. No one forced a second hypothesis and measured the result (gap 2 stays open). The 0.90 at k=0 is null-case specificity.
agent_relevance: A stop rule that refuses to submit while an untested rival remains is the cheapest untested fix. Expect it to trade omissions for hallucinated extras unless each rival needs a discriminating probe.

finding: Ablation shows keeping several candidate hypotheses alive is the largest single contributor in a tree-search RCA agent. Removing candidate batching costs 7.0 points, more than backpropagation or reflection. Gap 2 partial: breadth helps, but via search, not via a forced rival step before stopping.
numbers: LO2 benchmark accuracy: full 91.3; w/o candidate batching 84.3 (-7.0); w/o backpropagation 84.8 (-6.5); w/o reflection 87.6 (-3.7). Hypotheses explored 18.9 vs 5.1 (single ReAct) vs 8.5 (multi ReAct) at about 7.0 evidence items each.
limits: Single small benchmark (LO2). On 37 real incidents accuracy is 65.1 percent (see critique). Ablation is within-method, not against a plain sampling baseline.
agent_relevance: Hypothesis breadth, not evidence volume, drives the gain. A forced second hypothesis is a cheap version of this.

finding: Gap 5: the tree-search comparison is not token-matched. The best baseline used about half the tokens and lost by a wide margin, but no best-of-N or self-consistency baseline was run.
numbers: LO2: LATS-RCA 91.3 percent, 53.1 calls, 156K tokens, 9.1 min. ReAct single 39.8 percent, 13.5 calls, 41K tokens, 1.2 min. ReAct multi 57.4 percent, 25.2 calls, 73K tokens, 1.7 min. LATS uses 3.8x and 2.1x the tokens, 7.6x and 5.4x the runtime. A weaker backbone (GPT-5.2 nano) used 68.2 calls and 201K tokens yet scored lower.
limits: A 2.1x token ratio against a 34-point gap leaves open that ReAct with 2x budget or best-of-N would close part of it. More search tokens did not help weak backbones.
agent_relevance: Do not credit tree structure until a best-of-N arm with 156K tokens exists. Put that arm in our own test.

finding: Gap 5: in the Graph of States paper, bigger search topologies (ToT, GoT, FoT) cost far more and did not beat the structured method. Tree-of-thought was worse than chain-of-thought on Match, so more search structure alone was not better.
numbers: Medical task: GoS Match 31.88 (LLM judge) and 39.86 (human judge), $0.12 per case. Baselines (LLM/human): Single/ToT 21.01/24.64; Single/GoT 18.84/19.57; Multi/FoT 21.74/23.91 at $0.73 per case; best baseline human-judge about 26.09. Distributed-systems task: GoS Match 70.67 vs best baseline Multi/CoT 34.00; Multi/FoT $0.94 vs GoS $0.10 (about 8x cheaper). Ablation (LLM judge, GoS 31.88): w/o causal graph 18.12; w/o state machine 12.32, with cost up to $0.17 because the run exhausts the budget.
limits: LLM-judge and human-judge columns differ; read each against its own GoS value. No self-consistency or best-of-N baseline. The paper says GoS beats the baseline peak even with a restricted budget (sensitivity plot only).
agent_relevance: Cheap structure (explicit state, explicit stop rule) may matter more than tokens. The state machine also saves cost by ending runs.

source: Weng et al. (2025) Abduct, Act, Predict (A2P), arXiv 2509.10401
finding: Gap 1/7 indirect: a prompt-only three-step scaffold (infer hidden cause, define minimal fix, predict the result of the fix) run in one pass gives 2.4 to 2.9 times the step-level failure attribution of the all-at-once baseline. Removing the abduction step or the prediction step each loses points. Prediction (simulate then compare) matters most on the hard set.
numbers: Who&When step accuracy: Algorithm-Generated 47.46 vs 16.67 baseline (2.85x), best other baseline binary_search 28.57; Hand-Crafted 29.31 vs 12.07 (2.43x). Ablation: w/o abduction 41.11 (-6.35) and 20.69 (-8.62); w/o prediction 40.32 (-7.14) and 17.24 (-12.07); w/o step numbering 17.78 (-29.68). Formal causal criteria gave no significant gain (p 0.126 and 0.148). About 25 percent extra processing time.
limits: The paper states an AI system did about 95 percent of the work. One benchmark, one pass; the baseline is a prompt, not a token-matched sampler. Failure attribution in agent logs, not physical diagnosis.
agent_relevance: Supports an explicit 'predict what the repaired system would do, then compare' step in O8. A text scaffold can help when the log is given, unlike the Elenchos interacting case where evidence must be probed.

source: Halba, Cooper, Bellingham (2026) SPAR AUV fault recovery with LLMs, arXiv 2609.20620
finding: Gap 8: a physical-system diagnosis test (autonomous underwater vehicle, center-of-gravity shift injected in a closed-loop simulator). Model class dominates. The true cause appears in the top three far more often for the frontier model, and rank-one accuracy is lower than top-three for every model.
numbers: 480 trials (4 models x 3 prompt tiers x 2 magnitudes x 2 phases x 10 reps; n=40 per model-tier). Top-3 hit: gpt-5.5 85, 90, 85 percent (tiers 1-3); nemotron-nano-12b 78, 68, 60; gemma4:12b 42, 30, 38; gpt-oss:20b 10, 28, 25. Rank-one: gpt-5.5 75, 70, 43; nemotron 20-30; gemma 8-13; gpt-oss 0-5.
limits: One fault type, one simulator, single response with no loop. Tier confidence intervals overlap, so no prompt-tier effect is resolved. Gemma scored on final answers only.
agent_relevance: Top-k scoring hides weak ranking: rank-one drops 10 to 40 points. Score rank-one separately.

source: Halba, Cooper, Bellingham (2026) SPAR AUV fault recovery with LLMs, arXiv 2609.20620
finding: Gap 2 and 7 in a physical domain: the best local model followed the requested diagnostic procedure, tested several subsystems and kept competing hypotheses. Weaker models committed early to an elevator fault even though the elevator tracked its command, and extra equations after commitment did not help.
numbers: Static-stability material used substantively in 94 percent of nemotron trials vs 62 percent for gpt-oss. gemma4:12b inferred an elevator tracking error in several trials where the measured elevator followed its command. Diagnosis and the continue-or-abort decision did not appear coupled.
quote: Additional mathematical analysis did not improve diagnosis when the available evidence was not used to challenge the initial hypothesis.
limits: Qualitative, from final responses and some traces, not a controlled manipulation. Association only.
agent_relevance: Matches the Elenchos pattern. Math done after commitment is wasted. A rival-hypothesis check must come before the analysis step.

source: Gopal and Krishnan (2026) How Far Can Root Cause Analysis Go on Real-World Telemetry Data? arXiv 2607.13548
finding: Gap 7 cleaner test: evidence is computed once offline and given identically to every arm, then procedure and knowledge are varied separately. Knowledge rules help a lot. The prescribed five-step procedure text did not help, and its removal raised Full Score in all three conditions, though no contrast survives correction.
numbers: OpenRCA Market held-out cloudbed, Full Score: no rules 14.10; mined rules 35.90; manual rules 24.36; label-and-schema control 19.23. Mined rules fix 17 more cases on top of the procedure but 11 without it. Deleting only the earliest-onset criterion nets +8 cases vs +11 for removing the whole procedure. A second model (Gemma-4-31b-it) also gains.
limits: Small held-out set. Mining is label-conditioned. Only the abstract and the procedure sections were read closely.
agent_relevance: Domain knowledge in the prompt is worth more than a generic procedure; a rule that over-commits ('earliest anomaly wins') can hurt. Do not add rules that bias toward the first signal.

source: Qu et al. (2026) NeSy-CTM neurosymbolic clinical trial matching, arXiv 2606.20895
finding: Gap 3/4 neighbour: the LLM writes symbolic constraints (abduces missing facts) and a solver does the deterministic verification. That beat LLM-only reasoning and an abduction-free neurosymbolic variant, and was more robust to evidence noise.
numbers: Up to 30 percent relative gain over zero-shot. Average accuracy 75.71 percent. Only a 2 percent drop under controlled evidence perturbation vs 8.5 percent for the LLM-only approach. Zero-shot sensitivity 91.34 but specificity 24.66 (over-permissive). NeSy-CTM recovers 18 percent of cases where CoT fails; CoT succeeds on 12 percent where NeSy fails.
limits: Trial matching is constraint satisfaction, not fault finding. Three backbones averaged. Preprint.
agent_relevance: A code-side solver over model-proposed assumptions is a tested pattern. Complementarity with CoT suggests routing, not replacement.

source: Cotnareanu et al. (2026) PACS, probabilistic abductive commonsense, ICML 2026 / arXiv 2605.08011
finding: Gap 5 partial: an LLM plus a logic solver that samples many abductive proofs and aggregates them was compared to chain-of-thought and self-consistency with equal sample counts for independently sampled methods. A small non-thinking model with the search matched a 120B thinking model with self-consistency.
numbers: Table 4: self-consistency with GPT-OSS-120B (thinking) 82 percent on FOLIO and 80 on QUAIL; PACS with Llama 3.3 70B 88 and 84; PACS with Llama 3 8B 82 and 80. Cost control: equal samples for LoT and self-consistency; equal samples per step and beam width for search methods; CoT and LLM-Tres left unconstrained.
limits: Logical question answering, not fault diagnosis. Token cost not matched in the thinking-model comparison.
agent_relevance: Aggregation over sampled explanations with a solver is competitive with a bigger thinking model. A fair control for tree-search claims.

source: Reiter (1987); de Kleer and Williams (1987); Bylander et al. (1991); de Kleer, Mackworth, Reiter (1992), Crossref metadata only
finding: Gap 9 stays open. Only bibliographic records were read because publisher pages returned 403 and no open PDF was reachable. Citation counts confirm the papers are central, but formal claims K01-K03 are not checked against the text.
numbers: Crossref: Reiter AIJ 32(1) pp 57-95, 1,986 citing works; de Kleer and Williams AIJ 32(1) pp 97-130, 1,228; Bylander et al. AIJ 49 pp 25-60, 245; de Kleer-Mackworth-Reiter AIJ 56 pp 197-222, 322. No abstract field returned.
limits: Metadata only; opened is false because no paper text was read. Not verification of the formal results.
agent_relevance: Keep K01-K03 labelled as secondary-source claims until the papers are read.

source: Elenchos (2026) abductive-reasoning audit benchmark, arXiv 2607.12733 per-model table
finding: Gap 8, newest frontier models: the detection-attribution gap is present in all 13 models and is largest in the strongest detectors. Better detection does not mean better attribution.
numbers: Gap VK minus VA with paired bootstrap 95 percent CI: gemini-2.5-pro 0.57 [0.52, 0.63] (VK 0.93, VA 0.35); gemini-2.5-flash 0.53; gpt-5.4_low 0.52; gpt-5.4 0.50; claude-haiku-4-5 0.44; gpt-5.4_high 0.43; smallest 0.08 (ministral-8b, VK only 0.22). Overall VK 0.65, VA 0.28, VA given VK=1 0.39, gap 0.37 [0.35, 0.38]. Best VA is gpt-5.4_medium 0.47.
limits: Synthetic formal language with a 13-mutation ontology, not a real physical system; 5 reps per cell.
agent_relevance: Test detection and attribution apart; one does not predict the other.

source: Halba, Cooper, Bellingham (2026) SPAR AUV, arXiv 2609.20620 (operational side)
finding: Gap 8: diagnosis and the downstream action are separate failure modes. A model can diagnose better and act worse, so a diagnosis score is not a safe stand-in for an outcome score.
numbers: Manageable 0.005 m shift (continue is correct): gpt-5.5 continued correctly in 93 percent of cruise and 90 percent of descent trials; gpt-oss:20b 53 and 27 percent; nemotron 3 and 7 percent; gemma4:12b aborted every manageable-fault trial. Severe 0.05 m shift (abort is correct): gemma aborted every trial; nemotron 97 percent in cruise and 83 percent in descent; gpt-5.5 100 percent in cruise but 33 percent in descent.
limits: Ten reps per cell, one fault family. Nemotron had the best local diagnosis but the weakest decision on the manageable fault.
agent_relevance: Score the diagnosis and the action choice separately in any agent test.

finding: Gaps 1, 3, 6 and 10 found no direct study among the sources this pass could open. The shared WebSearch budget was exhausted and the arXiv, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs all returned HTTP 429 or a daily-budget error, so discovery of new papers was blocked. Absence of a found study is not proof none exists.
numbers: Opened this session: 8 arXiv PDFs (2607.12733, 2603.21250, 2605.03505, 2509.10401, 2609.20620, 2605.08011, 2607.13548, 2606.20895). Crossref metadata for 4 classic papers. 0 new WebSearch results.
limits: Search failure, not a finding about the literature.
agent_relevance: Run the matched tests ourselves: Ab-flag table vs prose (gap 1), hitting-set code loop (gap 3), probe-choice rule (gap 6).
